entities.name: Opioid use disorder
observations: Moderate-to-severe OUD is treated with opioid agonist or partial agonist medication, chiefly methadone or buprenorphine; medication treatment reduces withdrawal, cravings, illicit opioid use, and relapse risk.
Naltrexone requires adequate opioid abstinence before initiation and is not appropriate for a patient actively using opioids or currently physically dependent.

entities.name: Methadone
observations: An effective maintenance treatment for moderate-to-severe OUD that reduces opioid cravings and relapse risk; it is not limited to withdrawal treatment.

In the United States, methadone for OUD is generally dispensed through opioid treatment programs, with take-home flexibility for eligible patients rather than universally requiring daily supervised administration.

entities.name: Buprenorphine
observations: An effective first-line medication option for moderate-to-severe OUD and not categorically contraindicated by a history of liver disease; hepatic impairment requires clinical assessment and monitoring.
Hospitalized patients may receive buprenorphine for OUD without the former federal DEA X-waiver requirement; prescribing rules have changed and standard controlled-substance requirements apply.

entities.name: Naltrexone
observations: For selected patients with mild OUD who choose medication, naltrexone can be considered; however, it is not generally preferred over buprenorphine or methadone for moderate-to-severe OUD and cannot be started during active opioid use without an opioid-free interval.
